I will do it much like last year, because my land is only 3 mu and I cannot gamble. I have done wheat-maize for many years, and around here if the fertilizer is too little, the crop shows it fast and the yield drops. Wasting a little fertilizer hurts, but losing grain hurts more, so I will keep the base rate solid and only trim where I think I can save a bit. I watch what the better fields in the village do. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough bottom fertilizer, water from the well 3 times if the weather is normal, and spray 2 times if I see aphids, rust, or weeds getting ahead. For maize, I will use hybrid seed like most people do now, give it a heavier nitrogen hand than wheat, water 2 times if rain is short, and spray 2 times for weeds and insects. I do small-scale work with family labor, so I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and cheaper for my size than deep ploughing every time.
